claims.text: In their ancestral strongholds, Ancient Tzimisce kept apart from the mortal world, contemplating the horror within; the eldest sometimes walked among people and were worshipped as gods.
Endless experiments on the mortals they bred brought them knowledge but never understanding of humanity.
Their temples lay in cave mazes of the eastern Carpathian range, and the Methuselah Yorak made the grandest.
Yorak’s ghoul servants abducted mortals for the Methuselah to feed on, breed and finally shape into elaborate sculptures across the walls of a meditation chamber.
This is how the Cathedral of Flesh, close to the pass of the Red Tower, came to be.

title: The Black Churches
summary: Spiritualist temples of the earliest Transylvanian Tzimisce.

claims.text: The first Fiends in Transylvania were mystics, holding hidden rites contemplating the nature of abomination, having left human ways far behind.
By day their servants raised stone buildings above ground, while by night many-armed things dug tunnels beneath; these Black Churches still stand in many parts of Transylvania.
Vampire artisans finished the shrines below, raising uneven stone walls and, in the grander temples, walls made from sacrificed victims.

title: The Tremere-Tzimisce war
summary: How the conflict over Transylvania began.

claims.text: The Tzimisce resented Tremere chantries on lands they claimed, raiding the magi’s villages, supplies and sometimes the chantries themselves.
At first Hermetic wards held off the worst raids, and some regions were warded against the Tzimisce and their ghouls altogether, so the Fiends swore to find a way around the wizards’ magic.
Their chance came around the year 1000, when the Order of Hermes noticed reality itself shifting and disturbing the workings of magic.

title: Shaagra, Methuselah of Prague
summary: A fifth-generation Tzimisce who once led a Slavic tribe.

claims.text: Shaagra was mother goddess, war leader and shaman of a Slavic tribe, leading it west out of servitude and making a favourite granddaughter, Libussa, its ruler.
Passing through an ancient Tzimisce’s land, the tribe served that lord for a time; impressed, the elder Embraced Shaagra, bound the new childe by blood oath and sent Shaagra to claim new territory.

title: Vladimir Rustovitch
summary: A Tzimisce voivode holding out against the Tremere.

claims.text: Once a Bratovitch revenant, Vladimir took both Cainite status and the sire’s estate through effort, might and some treachery.
Vladimir has beaten jealous siblings and rival voivodes in Trials by War, and the growing fiefdom resists the Tremere.
Placed between western Hungary and war-torn Transylvania, Vladimir is strong enough to make Cainites of both sides respect the old traditions.

title: Princes of Prague and Buda-Pest
summary: Ventrue princes of two eastern cities.

claims.text: Rudolf Brandl, Prince of Prague, was the third son of a German noble house, trained as a knight and readied for the Church in case no landed marriage came.
Vencel Rikard, Prince of Buda-Pest, came to the city among Bavarian knights invited to guard King Geza and was Embraced by Bulscu as a reward for service.
Vencel cares most for keeping power, profiting from trade and keeping peace in a city where clans might go to war, and means to make Buda-Pest the greatest city of the region.
